deleted.title: If You Can Make It 1: The sandwich (bread, spread, and two ways to stand out)
deleted.hook: If you can make a sandwich, you can make something people pay for. Let me show you how.
deleted.notes:
Mercedes's idea 2026-10-30, the pilot. Her original hook: 'If you can make a sandwich, you can make $1K in the next 30 days.' Changed because the content rules say never promise $1,000 (and no timeline). Other safe options: 'you already know how to start your first $1K' / 'you can build your first $1K product'.

Beats: every sandwich needs bread and spread. Some are only bread and spread: PB&J. A staple, huge appeal, nothing different about it. Unless: (1) you cut it with a cookie cutter, think Uncrustables: the simplest thing, shaped the same way every time, so people recognise it; or (2) artisan ingredients, homemade bread and jam: same big-audience thing, quality you notice. Lesson: you don't need a new idea, you need a recognisable shape or noticeably better quality, done consistently.
Close: make something you love, share it with the world, and go after your next $1K.

Series rule: every episode = one thing people already know how to make + one business lesson, same closing line.

If You Can Make It 2: Crochet (one stitch, repeated)
deleted.hook: If you can crochet a granny square, you can build a business. Let me show you how.
deleted.notes: Lesson: consistency beats talent. A blanket is one simple stitch repeated hundreds of times; a business is one simple post or offer repeated. Then the pattern itself is a product: you can sell the hat, or sell the pattern and make it once (digital product). Same closing line as the series.

deleted.title: If You Can Make It 4: Pizza (same dough, different toppings)
deleted.hook: If you can make a pizza, you can sell to more than one kind of customer. Let me show you how.
deleted.notes: Lesson: one base product, different versions for different people (niches). Dough and sauce stay the same; the toppings change for the kid, the vegetarian, the spicy person. Keep the base, change the top, and name who each one is for.

deleted.title: If You Can Make It 5: Baking (follow the recipe backward)
deleted.hook: If you can follow a recipe, you can do the math for your first $1K. Let me show you how.
deleted.notes: Lesson: the $1K Math. A recipe starts from what you want (12 cookies) and works back to the ingredients. Same here: $1,000, then how many sales at your price, then visitors, then views (Playbook order; views are the output, not followers). Natural fit for the MATH keyword CTA (already live in Chat Manager). Don't pick a price to fit the goal: price comes first, the math only counts sales at that price.
